steps.note: The milk is warmed a little and left to set for about 24 hours.
The soft curd is ladled into long moulds.
It drains by itself in the moulds.
The unmoulded cheese is coated with salted, powdered charcoal.
It is turned daily in a cool, damp cellar for about 10 days.

processing.text: This is the way of Sainte-Maure de Touraine, a goat's cheese; the 24 hours, the cellar and the 10 days are as given there.

sources.text: The setting for 24 hours, ladling, salted charcoal and ripening in the cellar are from this page; it does not say how much rennet is used.
